subject.title: fix(gmail): stop watcher when OAuth renewal is invalid

question: Should a terminal Gmail OAuth renewal error immediately stop the active watcher and require reauthentication, rather than keep the listener running in a degraded state?
rationale: The linked issue establishes that stale healthy-looking coverage is wrong, but stopping the process is an upgrade-visible lifecycle choice rather than the only possible degraded-health design.

options.title: Stop on terminal OAuth
options.body: Adopt the PR's fail-closed behavior after live proof confirms terminal errors are classified narrowly and transient failures still retry.

options.title: Keep a degraded watcher
options.body: Require an explicit unhealthy status and bounded retry model while leaving the listener alive, which needs a broader design than this patch provides.

recommendation.title: Stop on terminal OAuth
recommendation.body: Adopt the PR's fail-closed behavior after live proof confirms terminal errors are classified narrowly and transient failures still retry.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail most directly connects kklouzal to the current Gmail watcher and foreground service lifecycle.
